For some \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&2\\1&2\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&\beta\end{bmatrix}\) be such that \(A^2-4A+2I=B^2-3B+I=O\). Then \(\left(\det\left(\operatorname{adj}(A^3-B^3)\right)\right)^2\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
By Cayley–Hamilton, \(A^2-(\alpha+2)A+(2\alpha-2)I=O\). Since \(A\) is not a scalar matrix, comparing with \(A^2-4A+2I=O\) gives \(\alpha=2\). Similarly \(1+\beta=3\), \(\beta-1=1\), so \(\beta=2\).
\(A^3=\begin{bmatrix}20&28\\14&20\end{bmatrix}\), \(B^3=\begin{bmatrix}5&8\\8&13\end{bmatrix}\), \(A^3-B^3=\begin{bmatrix}15&20\\6&7\end{bmatrix}\), \(\det=-15\).
For a \(2\times2\) matrix \(\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=\det M\), so the answer is \((-15)^2=225\).

questions.q: For the matrices \(A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-4\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B=\begin{bmatrix}-29&49\\-13&18\end{bmatrix}\), if \((A^{15}+B)\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\end{bmatrix}\), then among the following which one is true?
questions.sol:
\(N=A-I=\begin{bmatrix}2&-4\\1&-2\end{bmatrix}\) satisfies \(N^2=O\), so \(A^{15}=(I+N)^{15}=I+15N=\begin{bmatrix}31&-60\\15&-29\end{bmatrix}\).
\(A^{15}+B=\begin{bmatrix}2&-11\\2&-11\end{bmatrix}\), giving \(2x=11y\). Among the options only \(x=11,\ y=2\) works.

questions.q: If the system of equations \[3x+y+4z=3,\qquad 2x+\alpha y-z=-3,\qquad x+2y+z=4\] has no solution, then the value of \(\alpha\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}3&1&4\\2&\alpha&-1\\1&2&1\end{vmatrix}=3(\alpha+2)-3+4(4-\alpha)=19-\alpha\).
\(\Delta=0\Rightarrow\alpha=19\); for \(\alpha=19\), \(\Delta_x=\begin{vmatrix}3&1&4\\-3&19&-1\\4&2&1\end{vmatrix}\ne0\), so the system is inconsistent.

questions.q: If \(A=\begin{bmatrix}2&3\\3&5\end{bmatrix}\), then the determinant of the matrix \((A^{2025}-3A^{2024}+A^{2023})\) is:

Let \(A\) be a \(3\times3\) matrix such that \(A+A^T=O\). If \(A\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\3\\2\end{bmatrix}\), \(A^2\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-3\\19\\-24\end{bmatrix}\) and \(\det\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(2\operatorname{adj}(A+I)\right)\right)=2^\alpha\cdot3^\beta\cdot11^\gamma\), \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\) non-negative integers, then \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(A=\begin{bmatrix}0&a&b\\-a&0&c\\-b&-c&0\end{bmatrix}\). \(A(1,-1,0)^T=(-a,-a,c-b)^T=(3,3,2)^T\Rightarrow a=-3\).
\(A(3,3,2)^T=(-9+2b,\,9+2c,\,-3b-3c)^T=(-3,19,-24)^T\Rightarrow b=3,\ c=5\).
\(\det(A+I)=1+a^2+b^2+c^2=44\). For \(3\times3\): \(\det(\operatorname{adj}N)=(\det N)^2\) and \(\det(2\operatorname{adj}M)=8(\det M)^2\).
\(\det(\operatorname{adj}(2\operatorname{adj}(A+I)))=(8\cdot44^2)^2=2^{14}\cdot11^4\), so \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=14+0+4=18\).

If \(X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}\) is a solution of the system of equations \(AX=B\), where \(\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}4&2&2\\-5&0&5\\1&-2&3\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B=\begin{bmatrix}4\\0\\2\end{bmatrix}\), then \(|x+y+z|\) is equal to:

Among the statements:
I: If \(\begin{vmatrix}1&\cos\alpha&\cos\beta\\\cos\alpha&1&\cos\gamma\\\cos\beta&\cos\gamma&1\end{vmatrix}=\begin{vmatrix}0&\cos\alpha&\cos\beta\\\cos\alpha&0&\cos\gamma\\\cos\beta&\cos\gamma&0\end{vmatrix}\), then \(\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=\dfrac32\), and
II: If \(\begin{vmatrix}x^2+x&x+1&x-2\\2x^2+3x-1&3x&3x-3\\x^2+2x+3&2x-1&2x-1\end{vmatrix}=px+q\), then \(p^2=196q^2\),
questions.sol:
I: LHS \(=1-(\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma)+2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma\), RHS \(=2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos\gamma\), so the sum of squares is \(1\), not \(\tfrac32\): false.
II: Expanding (e.g. \(R_2\to R_2-R_1-R_3\) first), the determinant equals \(24x-12\). So \(p=24\), \(q=-12\) and \(p^2=576\ne196q^2=28224\): false.

\(\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\2&5&a\\1&2&3\end{vmatrix}=8-a\), so \(a=8\) gives \(\Delta=0\) (no unique solution).
For \(a=8\): \(R_2=-R_1+3R_3\) on the left side; consistency needs \(36=-6+3b\Rightarrow b=14\).

questions.q: Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}0&2&-3\\-2&0&1\\3&-1&0\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B\) be a matrix such that \(B(I-A)=I+A\). Then the sum of the diagonal elements of \(B^TB\) is equal to ______.
The number of \(3\times2\) matrices \(A\) which can be formed using the elements of the set \(\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}\) such that the sum of all the diagonal elements of \(A^TA\) is \(5\), is ______.
questions.sol:
\(\operatorname{tr}(A^TA)\) is the sum of the squares of all \(6\) entries, each square being \(0,1\) or \(4\).
Sum \(5=4+1\): positions \(6\cdot5\), signs \(2\cdot2\): \(120\). Sum \(5=1+1+1+1+1\): position of the zero \(6\), signs \(2^5\): \(192\).
Total \(=312\).

questions.q: Let \(P=[p_{ij}]\) and \(Q=[q_{ij}]\) be two square matrices of order \(3\) such that \(q_{ij}=2^{(i+j-1)}p_{ij}\) and \(\det(Q)=2^{10}\). Then the value of \(\det(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}P))\) is:
questions.sol:
\(2^{i+j-1}=2^i\cdot2^j\cdot2^{-1}\): row \(i\) is scaled by \(2^i\), column \(j\) by \(2^j\), and every entry by \(2^{-1}\).
\(\det Q=2^{6}\cdot2^{6}\cdot2^{-3}\det P=2^9\det P=2^{10}\Rightarrow\det P=2\).
\(\det(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}P))=(\det P)^{(3-1)^2}=2^4=16\).

questions.q: Let \(A,B\) and \(C\) be three \(2\times2\) matrices with real entries such that \(B=(I+A)^{-1}\) and \(A+C=I\). If \(BC=\begin{bmatrix}1&-5\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}\) and \(CB\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}12\\-6\end{bmatrix}\), then \(x_1+x_2\) is:
questions.sol:
\(C=I-A\) and \(B=(I+A)^{-1}\) are both functions of \(A\), so they commute: \(CB=BC\).
\(x_1-5x_2=12\), \(-x_1+2x_2=-6\Rightarrow x_2=-2\), \(x_1=2\); \(x_1+x_2=0\).

questions.q: Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-4\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B\) be two matrices such that \(A^{100}=100B+I\). Then the sum of all the elements of \(B^{100}\) is ______.
questions.sol:
\(N=A-I=\begin{bmatrix}2&-4\\1&-2\end{bmatrix}\) satisfies \(N^2=O\), so \(A^{100}=I+100N\Rightarrow B=N\).
\(B^{100}=O\), so the sum of its elements is \(0\).

questions.q: Let \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}\) be such that the system of linear equations \[x+2y+z=5,\qquad 2x+y+\alpha z=5,\qquad 8x+4y+\beta z=18\] has no solution. Then \(\dfrac\beta\alpha\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&2&1\\2&1&\alpha\\8&4&\beta\end{vmatrix}=12\alpha-3\beta=0\Rightarrow\beta=4\alpha\).
Then the LHS of the third equation is \(4\times\) the second, but \(18\ne4\cdot5\): no solution. So \(\tfrac\beta\alpha=4\).

questions.q:
Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\1&\alpha\end{bmatrix}\) and \(B=\begin{bmatrix}3&3\\\beta&2\end{bmatrix}\). If \(A^2-4A+I=O\) and \(B^2-5B-6I=O\), then among the two statements:
(S1): \(\left[(B-A)(B+A)\right]^T=\begin{bmatrix}13&15\\7&10\end{bmatrix}\) and
(S2): \(\det(\operatorname{adj}(A+B))=-5\),
questions.sol:
Cayley–Hamilton: \(1+\alpha=4\Rightarrow\alpha=3\); \(\det B=6-3\beta=-6\Rightarrow\beta=4\).
\((B-A)(B+A)=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\3&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4&5\\5&5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}13&15\\7&10\end{bmatrix}\); its transpose is \(\begin{bmatrix}13&7\\15&10\end{bmatrix}\), so (S1) is wrong.
\(\det(A+B)=20-25=-5\) and for \(2\times2\), \(\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=\det M\): (S2) is correct.

questions.q: If the system of equations \[x+5y+6z=4,\qquad 2x+3y+4z=7,\qquad x+6y+az=b\] has infinitely many solutions, then the point \((a,b)\) lies on the line:
questions.sol:
For infinitely many solutions the third equation must be \(p(\text{I})+q(\text{II})\): \(p+2q=1\), \(5p+3q=6\Rightarrow p=\tfrac97\), \(q=-\tfrac17\).
\(a=6p+4q=\tfrac{50}{7}\), \(b=4p+7q=\tfrac{29}{7}\). So \(a-b=3\).

Let \(S=\left\{A=\begin{bmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{bmatrix}:a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}\text{ and }A^2-4A+3I=O\right\}\) be a set of \(2\times2\) matrices. Then the number of matrices in \(S\), for which the sum of the diagonal elements is equal to \(4\), is:
questions.sol:
If \(\operatorname{tr}A=4\), Cayley–Hamilton gives \(A^2-4A+(\det A)I=O\), so the condition becomes \(\det A=3\): \(ad-bc=3\) with \(a+d=4\).
\((a,d)=(0,4),(4,0)\): \(bc=-3\), impossible. \((1,3),(3,1)\): \(bc=0\): \(9\) choices each. \((2,2)\): \(bc=1\): \(1\) choice.
Total \(=9+9+1=19\).

questions.q: Let \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&2\\-2&0&1\\1&3&5\end{bmatrix}\). Then the sum of all elements of the matrix \(\operatorname{adj}\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(2(\operatorname{adj}A)^{-1}\right)\right)\) is equal to:

\(|A|=-3+11-12=-4\), \((\operatorname{adj}A)^{-1}=\dfrac{A}{|A|}\), so \(B=2(\operatorname{adj}A)^{-1}=-\tfrac12A\) and \(|B|=-\tfrac18(-4)=\tfrac12\).
For \(3\times3\): \(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}B)=|B|\,B=-\tfrac14A\).
Sum of the elements of \(A\) is \(12\), so the answer is \(-3\).

Let \(A\) be a \(3\times3\) matrix such that \(A^T\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5\\2\\2\end{bmatrix}\), \(A^T\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\), \(A\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\4\\4\end{bmatrix}\) and \(A\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\3\\1\end{bmatrix}\). If \(\det(A)=1\), then \(\det\left(\operatorname{adj}(A^2+A)\right)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Row \(3\) of \(A\) is \((3,1,1)\) and row \(1\) is \((5,2,2)-(3,1,1)=(2,1,1)\); column \(3\) is \((1,3,1)^T\) and column \(1\) is \((3,4,4)^T-(1,3,1)^T=(2,1,3)^T\).
So \(A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1&1\\1&a&3\\3&1&1\end{bmatrix}\) with \(\det A=3-a=1\Rightarrow a=2\).
\(\det(A+I)=\begin{vmatrix}3&1&1\\1&3&3\\3&1&2\end{vmatrix}=8\). \(\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=(\det M)^2\) with \(\det(A^2+A)=\det A\cdot\det(A+I)=8\): answer \(64\).

questions.sol:
Infinitely many solutions of a homogeneous system \(\iff\Delta=0\):
\(\begin{vmatrix}1&2&t\\6&1&5t\\3&t^2&f\end{vmatrix}=-11f+t^3+27t=0\).
\(f(t)=\dfrac{t^3+27t}{11}\), \(f'(t)=\dfrac{3t^2+27}{11}>0\): strictly increasing.

questions.q: If \(f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}\) is defined by \[f(n)=\begin{vmatrix}n&-1&-5\\-2n^2&3(2k+1)&2k+1\\-3n^3&3k(2k+1)&3k(k+2)+1\end{vmatrix},\quad k\in\mathbb{N},\] and \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{k}f(n)=98\), then \(k\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Only the first column depends on \(n\), so \(\sum_{n=1}^kf(n)\) is the determinant with first column \(\left(\sum n,\,-2\sum n^2,\,-3\sum n^3\right)\).
Simplifying, \(\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^kf(n)=\frac{7k(k+1)(2k+1)}{6}=7\sum_{n=1}^kn^2\).
\(=98\Rightarrow\sum n^2=14\Rightarrow k=3\).

questions.q: Let \(M\) be a \(3\times3\) matrix such that \(M\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2\\3\end{bmatrix}\), \(M\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\\2\end{bmatrix}\) and \(M\begin{bmatrix}0\\0\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-1\\1\\1\end{bmatrix}\). If \(M\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1\\7\\11\end{bmatrix}\), then \(x+y+z\) equals:

The columns of \(M\) are the given images: \(x-z=1\), \(2x+y+z=7\), \(3x+2y+z=11\).
\(z=x-1\Rightarrow3x+y=8\), \(4x+2y=12\Rightarrow x=2\), \(y=2\), \(z=1\). Sum \(=5\).

Then \((\alpha-\beta)^2\) is equal to ______.

\(|A|=-1\). For \(3\times3\): \(\operatorname{adj}(\operatorname{adj}A)=|A|A=-A\) and \(\operatorname{adj}(A)\cdot(-A)=-|A|I=I\).
So \(A^2-\alpha A+\beta I=\text{RHS}\). \(A^2=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&1\\-1&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}\); comparing the \((1,2)\) entries: \(-1-\alpha=-2\Rightarrow\alpha=1\); the \((1,1)\) entries: \(2+\alpha+\beta=2\Rightarrow\beta=-1\).
\((\alpha-\beta)^2=4\).
